content.comment_body: Hello. I read somewhere that the new [product_name] might support cloud services. I'm curious if it's possible to update the firmware of my [product_name] [version_no] and get the same features as the latest version. Regards.

That won't be possible. The latest [product_name] version is a new generation of devices, and there won't be a firmware update for older [product_name] models to access new features. Otherwise, [company_name] would only need to release firmware updates instead of launching new hardware. Ultimately, [company_name] aims to sell new devices—would you do it differently?

Hello. Suppose you're working on a project and need three PLCs. After searching, you find two options. Company A, when introducing new features, creates a different model, and their older device can't be upgraded via firmware. Company B releases firmware updates so you get new features without replacing your existing PLC. Which company would you prefer? Regards.
That comparison isn't entirely fair. If Company B only did firmware upgrades, there would be no new models, and after some years, Company B might not be financially sustainable.
This is due to hardware limitations.
Hi, how could you change hardware just with a firmware update? If there are hardware changes needed, firmware alone won't upgrade it.
Exactly—that's what I mean. If the hardware allows it, why not add features through firmware? If not, then designing and producing a new device is necessary.
Are you certain that adding an extended web server feature is possible with just a firmware update for [product_name] [version_no], and doesn't require new hardware?

Most new firmware with advanced features also require hardware modifications to function. Personally, I might buy the newest device and use it as a gateway to the cloud. With [product_name] [version_no], you can transfer data across multiple units and upload to the cloud using a single newer device. That's just my suggestion.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the lack of ability to upgrade older [product_name] devices with new cloud-related features through firmware updates. There are comparisons to companies that enable feature upgrades via firmware, with disappointment that [company_name] requires buying new hardware for new features. The debate focuses on whether features should be available via firmware if the hardware allows, but [company_name] seems to tie new functionality to new device releases.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the option to upgrade older [product_name] models to access new cloud features through firmware updates, provided the hardware is compatible.
